property_summary: After a successful call to setOwner, the owner variable must always equal the _owner argument passed; the buggy version violates this by setting owner to address(0) regardless of the _owner argument.
The `setOwner` function must return `true` after successfully updating the owner; the buggy version violates this by returning `false` when called by the admin.
After a successful call to setOwner, the owner must equal the _owner argument; the mutant breaks this by leaving owner unchanged.
After any admin calls setOwner, the owner variable must equal the provided address argument; the bug breaks this by setting owner to msg.sender instead.

After admin calls setOwner, owner shows the effect of the `_owner` argument, not the caller; the mutant ignores the argument so for some inputs owner will equal msg.sender instead of _owner, violating this correlation.

After a successful setOwner call by the admin, the owner must equal the provided address argument for any non-zero distinct caller/argument pair; the bug sets it to msg.sender instead, so when sender != argument, owner will incorrectly equal sender.
For any admin caller and any distinct argument address, after a successful setOwner call, the owner must equal the provided argument; the mutant sets owner to msg.sender, violating this.

For any admin caller and any _owner argument, after a successful setOwner call, the return of the public getter owner() must be equal to the provided _owner argument; the mutant sets owner to msg.sender, so when msg.sender != _owner, owner() will incorrectly equal msg.sender.
After setOwner is called, the owner must equal the argument passed; the bug makes owner equal admin regardless of the argument, violating this rule when _owner != admin.

After calling setOwner with a new address, the owner state variable must equal the passed argument; the bug deletes that assignment, leaving owner unchanged, which violates the rule for any new address different from the current owner.
Only the admin can change the owner; the bug allows any caller to change it.
Only the original admin can change the value of owner; the bug allows any caller to change owner because the require statement passes unconditionally.
Any non-admin caller cannot change owner via setOwner; the mutant allows any caller to change owner.
Any caller who is not the current admin can never change the owner via setOwner; the mutant removes the onlyAdmin check allowing a non-admin to change it.
After a non-admin address interacts with C via setOwner, the owner state variable must not change from its initial value; the mutant allows a non-admin to change it.
For any caller, after calling setOwner, the owner must equal the caller if and only if the caller is admin; the mutant allows non-admins to become owner.

After any sequence of calls to setOwner, the owner remains the address set by the last successful call made from the immutable admin address; in the mutant, a non-admin can successfully change the owner.
Any successful call to setOwner must return true in the reference version, but the buggy version returns false.
For any msg.sender that passes the onlyAdmin check, the setOwner function MUST return true; in the buggy version it returns false.
